Feature variables represent variables that store values that are associated with
a feature in a specific sample. The describe e.g., the absolute or relative
abundance, the chromatographic retention time, the peak shape, or especially
when also processed data are imported, also properties like measurement
accuracy.

The feature variables can be accessed in MRMhub functions by either their
internal name, which always starts with `feature_` (e.g., `feature_intensity`)
or by their short names, such as `conc`, `intensity`, `norm_intesity`, and `rt`.

## Key Feature Variables

Following feature variables are essential for organizing the data processing
flow in `MRMhub`. The `intensity` variable corresponds to the raw signal (e.g.
peak area) of the analysis, which are retrieved from one of the original feature
variables (see below) All feature variables downstream are the result of data
processing, including those available in the MRMhub workflow. If raw, partial or
fully post-processed data is imported into MRMhub, e.g. via `import_data_csv()`,
the imported values must be assigned or match these variables names.

Many data processing and plotting functions in MRMhub use of these variables as
input variable. All of these variable are stored in the `dataset` table present
in the `MRMhubExperiment` object.

+--------------+----------------+---------------------------+--------------+

| Short Name   |                |                           |              |

|              |                | `height`, `response`, or  |              |
|              |                | `intensity` from the      |              |
|              |                | imported raw data. See    |              |
|              |                | below.                    |              |
+--------------+----------------+---------------------------+--------------+
| n            | fe             | Internal                  |              |
| om_intensity | ature_         | Standard-normalized raw   |              |
|              | norm_intensity | signal intensity          |              |
+--------------+----------------+---------------------------+--------------+

|              | ure_pmol_total | amount in the measured    |              |
|              |                | sample (pmoles/sample)    |              |

## Backup Feature Variables

Feature variables will be overwritten in some processing by re-calculated
values, i.e., feature area after interference correction, concentrations after
drift/batch correction or reference sample-based re-calibration. In these cases,
the original feature values are stored in a new 'backup' feature variable to
keep a record and allow exploring the variable at a later stage. Furthermore,
specific variables are created by some processing functions, e.g. during drift
correction the values of the curve (model fit) data points.

Also these variables are stored in the `dataset` table. The feature variable
name is based on the initial name with following postfixes:

+-------------+-------------+----------------------------------+-------------+
| Postfix of  | Examples    | Description                      |             |
| Variable    |             |                                  |             |
| Name        |             |                                  |             |
+=============+=============+==================================+=============+
| \_orig      | feature     | Currently, only used for the     |             |
|             | \_int       | backup \| before any             |             |
|             | ensity_orig | interference correction was \|   |             |
|             |             | applied. Corresponds always to   |             |
|             |             | the raw \| intensity values that |             |
|             |             | were imported \| into the        |             |
|             |             | `MRMhubExperiment` object.       |             |
+-------------+-------------+----------------------------------+-------------+
| \_raw       | f           | Corresponds to the raw (=        |             |
|             | eatu        | uncorrected) calculated features |             |
|             | re_conc_raw | values, i.e., before a new       |             |
|             |             | correction step was applied,     |             |
|             | featur      | such as drift/batch correction.  |             |
|             | e_in        |                                  |             |
|             | tensity_raw |                                  |             |
+-------------+-------------+----------------------------------+-------------+
| \_before    | feat        | Corresponds to the last          |             |
|             | ure_        | calculated value before a new    |             |
|             | conc_before | correction step was applied,     |             |
|             |             | i.e., drift/batch correction.    |             |
|             | feature_i   | For example, adjusted            |             |
|             | nten        | concentration after a drift      |             |
|             | sity_before | correction, before batch         |             |
|             |             | correction was applied.          |             |
+-------------+-------------+----------------------------------+-------------+
| \_beforecal | feature     | The non-calibrated raw or        |             |
|             | \_con       | adjusted concentration before    |             |
|             | c_beforecal | \`calibrate_by_reference()\` was |             |
|             |             | applied. Only applies to the     |             |
|             |             | concentration variable           |             |
+-------------+-------------+----------------------------------+-------------+
| \_fit       | conc        | Model fit data points calculated |             |
|             | _before_fit | by drift and batch correction    |             |
|             |             | functions. Use by `runscatter()` |             |
|             |             | to plot the trends.              |             |
+-------------+-------------+----------------------------------+-------------+

## Raw Feature Variables

The supported feature variables listed below characterize the features in
additional aspects. Import is that only of variables can be is used as "feature
raw intensity" for all data processing steps. This variable is then copied to
`intensity` after importing the data, by default `area` if available, or then
`height`, `response` or `intensity` in this order. The feature variable use for
`intensity` can also manually be set via \`set_intensity_var()\`

These variables are stored in the `dataset_orig` table, and are not being
modified by any MRMhub function. They are typically not available in MRMhub's
data processing functions, but plotting functions support some of these. The
support will be extended in upcoming versions.

+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| Variable     | Internal Name   | Description              |              |
| Short Name   |                 |                          |              |
| =======      | ========        | ========                 |              |
| ============ | =============== | ======================== |              |
| area         | feature_area    | Peak area                |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
|              |                 |                          |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| height       | height_height   | Peak height              |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| response     | height_response | Feature response (vendor |              |
|              |                 | specific)                |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| intensity    | fe              | Feature intensity        |              |
|              | ature_intensity | (vendor specific)        |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| rt           | feature_rt      | Retention time           |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| fwhm         | feature_fwhm    | Full Width at Half       |              |
|              |                 | Maximum Peak Height      |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| width        | feature_width   | Peak Width               |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| int_start    | fe              | Peak integration Start   |              |
|              | ature_int_start | Time                     |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| int_end      | feature_int_end | Peak Integration End     |              |
|              |                 | Time                     |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| symmetry \|  |                 |                          |              |
| feat         |                 |                          |              |
| ure_symmetry |                 |                          |              |
| \| Peak      |                 |                          |              |
| symmetry     |                 |                          |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| sn_ratio     | f               | Signal-to-Noise ratio    |              |
|              | eature_sn_ratio |                          |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| accuracy     | f               | Accuracy (often in       |              |
|              | eature_accuracy | reference to target      |              |
|              |                 | value)                   |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+
| ionratio     | f               | Ion ratio                |              |
|              | eature_ionratio |                          |              |
+--------------+-----------------+--------------------------+--------------+

QC type is represented with a consistent color scheme (both fill and line
colors) and specific point shapes in all plots generated by the MRMhub package.
This visual coding allows consistent identification and comparison of different
QC types across various visualizations.
